title: Transport of open-site stalk coordinates under further restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in U$ an open neighbourhood, and $S_A$ the module stalk functor on the slice site over $A$, with scalars restricted to $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor]. Write $R_{BA}$ for slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. One can choose, before any modules or maps, natural isomorphisms $e_W:R_{WU}S_W\cong S_U$ for all $x\in W\subseteq U$. For every $x\in W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ and every natural isomorphism $a:R_{VU}S_V\cong S_U$, there exist natural isomorphisms $c:R_{VU}R_{WV}\cong R_{WU}$ and $d:R_{WV}S_W\cong S_V$ such that for every module sheaf $M$ on the U slice, $S_W(c_M)e_{W,M}=d_{R_{VU}M}a_M$. No finite free source or prescribed map is assumed, and no neighbourhood or lifting morphism is produced.

source.place: Sheaves Tag 00A0 (3), (5), lemma-restrict; Sheaves Tag 0096, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules. Read https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00A0 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0096 on 2026-10-13. The coordinate extension calculation is the naturality and adjunction triangle argument written by T3.

proof.text: For every x in W contained in U, take the explicit natural isomorphism e_W given by Scheme.openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison. The choice is made for all W before introducing V, a, or any module. Iterated slice restriction R followed by Q is naturally isomorphic to direct restriction P: the component is the identity because overMap evaluates at the same composite inclusion; naturality is reflexivity. No canonical germ-composition law is needed.

Transport the Mathlib adjunction Modules.restrictAdjunction through Modules.overEquiv U and Modules.overEquiv V, using overMapCompOverEquiv. Its right adjoint J is the composite of the V site equivalence, open-immersion pushforward, and the inverse U site equivalence. All three are fully faithful, hence J is fully faithful and the transported adjunction has invertible counit epsilon.

For any adjunction R left adjoint to J with invertible counit epsilon, an isomorphism t:R F to R G descends to d:F to G by the composite F(epsilon inverse), t whiskered by J, G(epsilon). Naturality supplies d. At R M, the triangle identity identifies epsilon inverse with R(unit_M), and naturality of t at unit_M gives d_(R M)=t_M. Apply this elementary calculation with F=Q followed by the W stalk, G=the V stalk, and t=the associator inverse followed by the W-stalk image of c, followed by e_W, followed by a inverse. The component formula and cancellation a inverse followed by a equals identity give the required equality. The calculation covers equal opens and zero modules; x in W excludes an empty W.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_openStalk_restriction_transport
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U) :
    ∀ (V : X.Opens) (hxV : x ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U)
      (a : SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE hVU) ⋙
        openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩ ≅ openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩)
      (W : X.Opens) (hxW : x ∈ W) (hWV : W ≤ V) (hWU : W ≤ U),
      let R := SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hVU)
      let Q := SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hWV)
      let P := SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hWU)
      ∃ (c : R ⋙ Q ≅ P)
        (d : Q ⋙ openModuleStalkFunctor X W ⟨x, hxW⟩ ≅
          openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩),
        (∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U),
          c.hom.app M = 𝟙 _) ∧
        ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U),
          (openModuleStalkFunctor X W ⟨x, hxW⟩).map (c.hom.app M) ≫
              (openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison X U W hWU x hxU hxW).hom.app M =
            d.hom.app (R.obj M) ≫ a.hom.app M
